tests.item: Outreach contacts reconcile to 50 (15 strategic, 35 financial)

Double counting means a separate June Contact row for a named party on top of a cohort Count that already includes it, or cohort Counts larger than the remainder, so that the rows sum past 50 without acknowledgment. Contacts are not entries: no Rounds line or Note counts the 50 as admitted bidders.
tests.expected: 50 approached = 15 Strategic (Party A, CSC [recorded as CSC/Pamplona], 13 others) + 35 Financial. Contacts are not entries. The sequence implies Party B and Party C were among the 35, but the filing does not state it, so netting them out of the financial cohort and leaving it at 35 (or 34-35) are both accepted.
tests.partial_credit: Totals and type split right, but one named party counted twice in the stated arithmetic (e.g. a June Party A Contact row plus a 15-strategic cohort that includes it; or separate Party B/Party C Contact rows plus a disjoint 35-financial cohort summing to 52 with no Note on the overlap). Also partial: the strategic/financial split is missing, or the rows are right but a Rounds line or Note treats contacted parties as admitted.
accepted_alternatives: Financial cohort qualified as 'Count: 34-35' with Count blank, because '50 parties, including CSC and Pamplona' leaves open whether CSC and Pamplona were counted as two entities
Strategic remainder qualified (e.g. 'Count: 12-13') under a two-entity reading of CSC and Pamplona, with the reasoning in the Note
One aggregate Contact row for all 50 with the 15/35 split in Who or Note, saying Party A and CSC/Pamplona are included, provided no separate June row adds them again

Strategic cohort Count 14 or 15 that expressly includes Party A (Note: first contacted 04/08), with CSC/Pamplona inside or outside it, provided the stated arithmetic reaches 50 with each named party once
Named Contact rows for Party B, Party C and CSC/Pamplona inside a netted residual (e.g. 33 other financial) summing to 50
Financial Contact cohort kept at 35 (or 'Count: 34-35'), with a Note that Party B and Party C are presumably but not expressly among them
The 04/08 first contact labelled Contact (target-initiated) instead of Target interest; the label is not scored here
tests.source_quote: 50 parties, including CSC and Pamplona, who together we refer to as CSC/Pamplona, and Party A, to solicit potential interest in a transaction with Mac-Gray, 15 of which were potential strategic buyers and 35 of which were potential financial buyers
provenance: verifier (source fidelity): B/C membership in the 35 not stated

tests.item: Closure of the 16 unnamed financial NDA signers without false timing precision
tests.check: Read the Deal ledger exit row(s) for the 16 unnamed financial NDA signers, with Rounds R1 and the Questions. (a) The 16 are closed exactly once in total: Counts or ranges reconcile to 16, with no second closure at signing; Inferred = Y; Exit reason Not stated. (b) The closure does not assert as fact that all 16 were eligible for the 07/23/2013 due date or live at the 07/25/2013 selection. (c) The timing uncertainty is stated in the Note and/or a Question. Note for graders: the filing says NDA signers were furnished a package with indications due by 07/23, but the 20 NDAs were signed 'over the next two months' after 06/24 and Party A (one of the 20) signed on 08/05; this does not establish that the other 16 had signed by 07/23, so an exact all-16 closure at 07/23 or 07/25 is over-precise under Part B. That textual argument is why such a closure earns partial credit when caveated, not a pass.
tests.expected: One inferred Dropped by target row: Count 16, Exit reason Not stated, Inferred Y. It is bounded at a later complete-set transition on or after the end of the roughly two-month NDA window: by 08/27/2013 (letter to only the four) or by 09/11/2013 (final request to only the four). The Note says each member's signing date, 07/23 eligibility and actual exit are unknown.
tests.partial_credit: Partial: the cohort is closed once with Count 16 and Inferred Y, but as an exact all-16 closure at 07/23 (Did not submit), 07/25 (Dropped by target) or 08/15 (the authorization naming only the four, still inside the roughly two-month signing window), AND the Note or a Question explicitly says that members' signing dates or 07/23 eligibility are unknown (e.g. citing Party A's 08/05 signing). Also partial: a supported later bound with an Exit reason other than Not stated; a later bound labelled Did not submit (the 16 were not solicited on 08/27 or 09/11); or closure only as Not selected at signing by 10/14/2013. Fail: the same exact 07/23, 07/25 or 08/15 all-16 closure with no acknowledgment that members may have signed later; or the cohort never closed, closed twice, given a reported (non-inferred) exit or a withdrawal/valuation reason; or all 20 signers carried live into round 2.
accepted_alternatives: Dropped by target by 08/27/2013
Dropped by target by 09/11/2013
Dropped by target by 09/24/2013 (exclusivity), if the Note explains that no member was among the named four
A split closure that keeps each part's Count blank or qualified (e.g. 'Count: 0-16' Did not submit by 07/23, remainder dropped by 08/27 or 09/11), reconciling to 16 without overlap
Exit row in Round 1 (the round left) or in the round of the bound date; the round number is not scored
tests.source_quote: Over the next two months a total of 20 potential bidders, including two strategic bidders (Party A and CSC/Pamplona) and 18 financial bidders (including Party B and Party C), entered into confidentiality agreements with Mac-Gray
provenance: v1.13 baseline #22 and raw v1.13.2 #23: all 16 Did not submit by 07/23
verifier (conformance): caveated vs uncaveated exact closure separated
